PullRequest.Title: agentHost: exclude external sessions from Mission Control
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

External Copilot-app sessions can be hidden from the local session list while still being published to Mission Control. Exclude all sessions marked external from Mission Control publishing, independently of `chat.agentSessions.showExternal`.

- Filter session discovery responses and live catalogue additions/updates on the Mission Control listener.
- Exclude external sessions from AHP action mirroring and SDK history/live-event replication.
- Preserve local, SSH, and tunnel listings and allow explicitly adopted sessions to become eligible once their external flag is cleared.
- Send a full catalogue addition when adoption makes a previously filtered session visible to an existing connection.
- Add regression tests for native/legacy session URIs, restored/surfaced summaries, current provenance, and adoption; document the sharing boundary.

This does not delete sessions previously published to Mission Control or change authenticated access to known resources.

Live Mission Control/mobile service verification was not run locally.

## Manual verification

With an external Copilot-app session loaded locally and remote connections enabled, confirm it is absent from the Mission Control session list and does not create a mirrored task. Changing the local external-session visibility setting must not change that result. Confirm a native VS Code session still appears, and an explicitly adopted external session becomes eligible.

(Written by Copilot)

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The allocation, insertion sites, sole deletion site, connection lifetime, and 100-item archived rotation are all directly visible in the traced code. Exact heap impact depends on host lifetime, catalogue churn, and client count, so severity is low, but the monotonic retention mechanism is certain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Per-client Set entries and retained session resource strings
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Retained entries grow with every distinct session ever returned or announced during a connection, multiplied by the number of connected Mission Control clients, rather than with the current effective catalogue (all non-archived sessions plus 100 archived sessions).
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Long-lived agent hosts retain steadily growing per-client hash tables, increasing heap use and GC pressure as sessions are created and archived.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR, protocol clients had no knownSessionSummaries Set, so repeated Mission Control listings did not retain a per-client history of session identifiers.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Each filtered-listener connection now records every session resource sent by listSessions or sessionAdded and keeps it until the underlying session is explicitly removed or the connection closes.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added loop at lines 2184-2187 inserts every listed resource into client.knownSessionSummaries; the diff only deletes entries on root/sessionRemoved at line 3808. Sessions that merely age out of toMissionControlSessionList's 100-archived-session window are never removed from the Set.
Findings.Title: Evict summaries that leave the client catalogue
Findings.Impact: With a persistent Mission Control connection and ongoing session creation/archival, agent-host memory grows linearly with catalogue history; multiple connected clients duplicate the retained hash entries and add GC pressure even though only 100 archived sessions remain listable at a time.
Findings.Evidence: toMissionControlSessionList returns all non-archived summaries and only the 100 most recently modified archived summaries, so normal archive churn causes different IDs to enter the response over time. The new Set is populated from each response and from sessionAdded, but it is not reconciled against later authoritative list results; root/sessionRemoved is the only per-entry deletion. Thus a persistent connection retains the union of all historical result sets, not the current capped set.
Findings.Recommendation: Track only summaries that were suppressed and need an adoption add, or reconcile known entries by list generation while preserving sessionAdded notifications that arrive during the async list computation, so retained state is bounded by the client's current catalogue.

Scenarios.Scenario: A Mission Control client requests listSessions repeatedly while sessions are created and archived
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The request awaits AgentService.listSessions, visibility/grant checks, summary preparation and filtering, the Mission Control archived-session projection, and response serialization/send. The new Set insertion loop is synchronous on this critical path after the catalogue is prepared.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enumerate the registry and bulk-read central catalogue metadata, with provider/session-storage fallback work for misses.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One coalesced catalogue computation per mode/epoch; one bulk central read for eligible candidates, with fallback work governed by existing catalogue eligibility.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same AgentService.listSessions computation was required before the PR; the new summary filter runs only after it completes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The list response waits for this work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the listSessions JSON-RPC response over the protocol transport.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One response per request containing the post-filter effective catalogue.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A response was already sent; the diff reduces its payload by excluding external summaries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Completes the client request after projection.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The computation scales with the registered session catalogue; the response contains all eligible non-archived sessions plus at most 100 archived sessions. The retained Set scales instead with the union of all distinct summaries returned over the connection lifetime, multiplied by connected clients.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The underlying list computation is coalesced per mode. Per-request projection remains serialized in the request handler after the shared result resolves; directory visibility checks use Promise.all where applicable. Each client owns an independent Set.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Concurrent AgentService.listSessions calls for the same external-session mode coalesce through _inFlightListSessions, with one trailing recomputation after invalidation. Set.add deduplicates repeated identical listings, but there is no generation eviction when the capped archived window rotates and no negative cache relevant to the filter.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the diff adds per-client Set insertion for every returned summary, while only root/sessionRemoved deletes entries and the archived-list adapter rotates a capped window.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Heap growth depends on connection lifetime, session/archive churn, automatic deletion, and client count; this uncertainty lowers the retained-state finding to low severity.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable low-severity retained-memory regression: the per-client index grows with historical catalogue membership instead of the current effective list.

Scenarios.Scenario: Session additions and summary changes are broadcast to connected Mission Control clients, including external-session adoption
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A state-manager catalogue notification is synchronously projected once per active client, then eligible notifications are sent through that client's transport. External summaries now stop before send; an adopted summary not present in knownSessionSummaries is projected as one full sessionAdded notification.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send a root/sessionAdded or root/sessionSummaryChanged notification to each eligible protocol client.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one send per active client per catalogue notification; external summaries produce zero sends, and first adoption can produce one full add per client.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The per-client send boundary already existed. The diff suppresses external notifications and changes the first eligible adoption update from a delta to one full addition.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Projection and enqueueing occur inline with notification broadcast; network delivery is transport-managed.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost scales with active client count per catalogue event. Full-add payload size scales with one session summary and its visible chats; there is no collection-wide fan-out beyond the existing per-client broadcast.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Projection and transport.send calls occur synchronously in one loop over active clients; downstream transport queuing governs actual I/O. No new Promise.all burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: knownSessionSummaries acts as per-connection membership state. Membership is warm after a list or sessionAdded, resets on reconnect, and is removed only on root/sessionRemoved; external negative state is not separately cached.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the broadcast loop, membership checks, recursive adoption projection, and transport send are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical connected-client count and summary/chat payload size are not established, but the changed external filter reduces ordinary boundary traffic.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional reportable latency or network regression; the one full add on adoption is bounded and required, while external notification traffic is reduced.

Scenarios.Scenario: AHP actions from local sessions are mirrored to Mission Control
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Every emitted envelope resolves its owning session and checks the current summary. External sessions now return before publisher.enqueue; eligible sessions continue through project registration, serialization/chunking, bounded spool admission, and relay publication.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve repository root and fetch remotes when registering a cold eligible session for mirroring.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most once per publisher session registration, not per action after warm registration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: External and internal sessions could both reach project resolution before the PR; the new guard removes external calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Initial actions buffer until registration resolves; external sessions now avoid this boundary.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Publish serialized/chunked AHP mirror frames to the Mission Control relay.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Frames scale with eligible action count and chunked payload size under existing frame/byte limits; external sessions now produce zero frames.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The relay boundary already existed and external actions reached it; the diff suppresses that traffic.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Admission/serialization occurs inline, while relay acknowledgement is handled by the bounded mirror queues.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One admission check per emitted envelope. For eligible sessions, work scales with action frequency and payload bytes; external actions now generate zero publisher registrations or mirror frames.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Mirror publication is independently ordered per session/namespace and globally bounded by the existing relay limits; project registration is shared by the per-session publisher entry. The diff introduces no burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Publisher registration is cached per session. Cold eligible sessions may resolve repository project metadata; warm registered sessions enqueue directly. The new external check is a current-state lookup rather than a cached decision, allowing adoption to become eligible.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added predicate precedes publisher.enqueue and sdk.observeSession in the traced event callback.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: External action frequency and cold repository-resolution latency vary, but all changed effects on this path reduce work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression; the change removes external-session filesystem/serialization/network work from this path.

Scenarios.Scenario: SDK history reconciliation and live-event replication at startup and after adoption
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Construction scans loaded session URIs and observeSession performs cheap eligibility checks. Eligible sources enter a Limiter(4), register the session, read/write sequence and journal metadata, replay provider history, serialize live events, and enqueue relay frames. External sessions now return before source allocation and all boundaries; adoption permits the existing path on the next observation/event.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open session storage and read/write SDK sequence and journal cursor metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Cold eligible source reads sequence/cursor metadata and writes a reservation; reservations recur per 1,024 sequence range and cursor writes follow acknowledged progress. External sources now make zero calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: External sessions previously reached these existing database operations; the added guard suppresses them.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These operations precede history/live publication for that source but run off the local AHP dispatch path under Limiter(4).

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read provider-native historical chat session events through an async iterator.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One history stream per cold eligible source, then event-by-event replay from its cursor; external sources now have none.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: External sessions were previously reconciled; the diff prevents that read.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: History reconciliation blocks that source's live drain but not local AHP dispatch and is limited globally to four sources.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enqueue SDK mirror events for relay publication.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One bounded frame per admitted eligible SDK event; external sessions now produce zero frames.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This existing boundary accepted external events before the PR; they are now filtered.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Frame admission occurs in the source drain; downstream relay backpressure can delay replay but is off the local action critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Startup checks scale with loaded sessions, while expensive work scales only with eligible sessions and their history/live event counts. History yields every event with a cooperative timeout every 10,000 events; live queues are bounded by 256 events, 2 MiB per session, and 32 MiB total.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Historical/drain work is globally limited to four source operations. Each source has one draining promise, coalescing repeated observations and live events; mirror queues apply downstream byte/frame backpressure.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Per-session sources retain sequence reservations, cursors, and a bounded seen-event set. Sequence metadata is reserved in blocks of 1,024; warm sources avoid repeated registration and usually avoid reservation I/O until the range nears exhaustion. External sessions do not create negative-cache entries, so adoption is discovered from current summary state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the new external predicate executes before SourceSession creation, limiter scheduling, database access, provider history iteration, and mirror enqueue.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider history sizes and adoption frequency vary, but limiter, queue caps, cursor behavior, and changed eligibility are explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression; startup and live replication work are reduced for external sessions, and adopted sessions pay the pre-existing bounded cold-start cost once eligible.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all seven changed files and traced listing, catalogue broadcast/adoption, AHP mirroring, and SDK history/live replication. Reported one low-severity unbounded-retention issue in the new per-client known-summary index; all changed expensive-boundary effects otherwise suppress work or remain bounded and unchanged.
